# 2. Player Experience and Game Flow

2.1 Core Loop Observe the environment and listen for the predator -> choose a route and movement pace -> search for clues, silver, gunpowder, odor supplies or puzzle objects -> solve or advance an environmental puzzle -> evade, hide from, mask against, or temporarily neutralize the werewolf -> reach a safe haven or unlock a new route -> repeat until the final escape condition is completed.

2.2 Player Verbs Verb Player-facing result Risk / cost Walk Move quietly at normal pace and preserve stamina. Leaves a normal scent trail. Crouch Move cautiously and reduce visible profile/noise. Slower traversal; exact scent reduction TBD. Short sprint Create immediate distance, evade a pounce sideways, or cross an exposed space. Consumes stamina; after a threshold, produces a stronger, longer-lasting scent trail. Contextual vault Cross selected low obstacles without a parkour system. Creates movement commitment and likely noise; exact interactions TBD. Interact / inspect Open doors, examine clues, operate mechanisms, collect items and use puzzle objects. May require standing still or expose the player; interruption rules depend on the puzzle. Hide Enter authored hiding places and wait for the werewolf to search or leave. Without active odor masking, the werewolf tracks the scent to the hiding place and pulls the player out. Apply odor Use perfume, cologne or absinthe on the player to weaken the scent trail. Finite consumable; direct sight and nearby sound remain relevant. Aim / fire Use the rifle or handgun to stagger or knock the werewolf unconscious. Consumes one silver ball and one gunpowder charge; every shot is permanent until a save reload. v0.2 | CONCEPT / PRE-PRODUCTION | PAGE 3 Verb Player-facing result Risk / cost Reload Prepare the single-shot firearm for the next defensive use. Long real-time vulnerability; weapon-specific movement restrictions. Carry large object Transport selected puzzle items or containers through the environment. Occupies the hands and prevents firearm use.

2.3 Session Arc Phase Player experience System focus Opening / orientation Learn movement, interaction, basic layout and the immediate escape problem. The werewolf is first suggested, then demonstrated. Exploration readability; scent premise; first safe-haven discovery. Early game Enter the first major area,define avenue in which clues are offered for defensive systems and goal via notes, hints or character dialogue Hiding, odor masking, first pounce, first firearm use. Mid-game Open multiple connected areas, revisit earlier rooms, solve puzzles to progress, and decide when scarce resources justify optional exploration. Persistent search, stronger scent from sprinting, resource economy, shortcuts and path openings. Late game The player understands the environment and predator, but objectives require longer trips through exposed routes. More frequent line-of-sight encounters, charge pressure, extended puzzle chains. Final escape Complete the last environmental condition and survive a final traversal or pursuit toward an exit the werewolf cannot follow. Alternative ending under evaluation TBD All learned systems; water boundary may become narratively and mechanically relevant. Werewolf cannot swim

2.4 Failure, Saving and Recovery
- Capture: Contact or a successful pounce results in immediate failure; there is no conventional health bar currently planned.
- Saving: Autosave only, triggered inside true safe havens.
- Reloading a save: Restores the complete saved world state, including puzzle progress, resource use and werewolf state recorded at that save.
- Expedition tension: Progress since the last safe haven is lost on capture, so spacing must create tension without excessive repetition.
- Safe-haven reset: Entering a safe haven ends the active pursuit and resets the werewolf to a randomized patrol state.
